title: Calculator: XR three-flow analysis for an independent rebuild

sections.title: Identity, package, permissions and local data

findings.claim: The inspected target is Calculator 1.0.0 (build 1.0) on iPhone XR / iOS 16.1.1
findings.explanation: The USB inventory identifies com.apple.calculator; all three original UI investigations verified that Bundle ID in the foreground. The acquired package reports version 1.0.0, build 1.0.
findings.limitation: No iOS 17 or iOS 26 run was performed.

findings.claim: The installed Calculator package contains one 361,440-byte Mach-O and no bundled extension or framework
findings.explanation: The captured IPA has 11 file entries, one executable with SHA-256 8d4e059834d4c3df36f2b5ba473863b55230cb21c7eeeee7919cafdb0dc7ff3c, no bundled frameworks and no extensions. The binary has no encryption load command; requested package recovery made no code replacement.
findings.limitation: This is an analysis snapshot of the installed system App. No encryption load command does not generalize to App Store Apps.

findings.claim: The main executable links 30 dynamic libraries, including UIKit, Foundation, private Calculate, AppSupport and Swift runtime libraries
findings.explanation: The Mach-O load-command index lists these dependencies. The Objective-C metadata index contains 16 local classes and 112 methods, including CalculatorModel, CalculatorController, DisplayValue and CalculatorWindow.
findings.limitation: A link does not prove that one selected gesture executed a library function; Objective-C metadata is not a full Swift type or call graph.

findings.claim: The USB inventory lists five entitlement keys and the sandbox index lists 18 paths
findings.explanation: The entitlement keys include platform-application, system-application, container-required and secure-mode. The metadata-only sandbox index includes Library/Preferences/com.apple.calculator.plist and saved-state paths.
findings.limitation: Values and file contents were not read; these paths do not establish which selected action wrote data.

sections.title: Three newly authored and device-replayed behaviors

findings.explanation: The new bounded playbook clears the prior result, enters 0.1, taps add, enters 0.2 and taps equals. The final UIKit label and saved image show 0.3; the screenshot gate also confirmed the visible keypad.
findings.limitation: This single run does not establish arbitrary decimal precision, rounding policy or expression history.

findings.claim: Applying plus/minus to 9 and then adding 2 displays −7
findings.explanation: The new flow clears state, taps 9, plus/minus, add, 2 and equals. The final UIKit label is the Unicode minus sign followed by 7, and the saved screenshot agrees.
findings.limitation: The flow does not test multiple sign toggles, negative zero or expression history.

findings.claim: The percent key transforms 50 into 0.5 in the selected state
findings.explanation: After clearing state and entering 50, percent produces a final UIKit label and screenshot of 0.5 without pressing equals.
findings.limitation: Percent with a pending operator, repeated percent or other magnitudes may follow different rules.

findings.claim: The clear control changes its accessibility label between clear and all clear depending on Calculator state
findings.explanation: Before scripting, the active result exposed clear; after a fresh launch, the same top-left control exposed all clear. The accepted scripts use its observed fixed center at (58, 383), and each resulting replay passed foreground and step checks.
findings.limitation: The exact C/AC state machine and behavior after every operation were not exhaustively tested.

sections.title: Main UI construction and keypad layout

findings.claim: CalculatorController builds a root view from separate display and keypad controller views
findings.explanation: The exact-binary loadView entry at 0x100004c80 directly calls 0x100004ad0. That helper obtains displayController.view and keypadController.view and sends addSubview: for each on the root view. The saved UIKit tree and screenshots independently show a result area above the keypad on the XR.
findings.limitation: The decompiler output is a static interpretation of the installed binary. The current three tap traces target CalculatorModel rather than these loadView functions, so they do not time their execution.

findings.claim: CalculatorKeypadView lays out a button array in a five-row grid and gives the zero key a spanning frame in basic mode
findings.explanation: The exact-binary layoutSubviews entry at 0x1000219fc directly calls 0x100021510. The helper reads buttons and keypadType, iterates five rows, computes frames, and sends setFrame: to each button. Its special row-4 branch combines two CGRect values with CGRectUnion before setting the frame. The current XR image shows the wide zero key on the bottom row.
findings.limitation: Ghidra does not recover every Swift value and frame formula cleanly; the alternate keypad branch and layout on other device sizes have not been dynamically tested.

findings.claim: DisplayViewController constructs a dark result view and registers swipe, long-press and double-tap gesture recognizers
findings.explanation: The exact-binary loadView entry at 0x1000286c0 calls 0x1000283a4, which obtains a lazy display view, installs it with setView:, sets systemBlackColor, and adds UISwipeGestureRecognizer, UILongPressGestureRecognizer and a two-tap UITapGestureRecognizer. The lazy builder at 0x100027e68 stores the created view. The Objective-C index also lists swipe:, longPress: and doubleTap: on DisplayViewController.
findings.limitation: The three accepted arithmetic flows did not exercise these gestures. Their exact user-visible effects, gesture conflicts and copy/paste behavior remain unverified.

sections.title: Runtime dispatch and bounded code interpretation

findings.claim: The CalculatorModel::buttonPressed: current IMP and original binary entry each fired once per selected tap window
findings.explanation: The current three-flow Frida traces record one hit for both hooks at each tap, including clear, decimal, digits, sign, add, equals and percent. Raw low-32-bit argument values are preserved beside step indices.
findings.limitation: A bounded temporal hit does not prove all downstream effects, and the value meaning requires UI/button binding.

findings.claim: A same-binary dispatcher branches on raw button values to separate entry points
findings.explanation: The current trace observes 51 for clear; 10 for decimal; 12, 13 and 20 for digits; 3 for sign; 8 for add; 9 for equals; 4 for percent. The verified Ghidra output for the exact 8d4e0598… binary shows buttonPressed: calling 0x10000e9b8, whose switch maps these values to bounded helper entries including 0x100014840, 0x10000f09c, 0x10000eb5c, 0x10001136c and 0x10001266c.
findings.limitation: The Ghidra run and current phone replay were collected at different times. Static branch selection and matching hit windows do not establish the internal Calculate framework algorithm or a complete call sequence.

findings.claim: The 0x10000f09c helper touches displayValue and enteringDecimal, but its full semantics are unresolved
findings.explanation: The same-hash direct Ghidra pseudocode shows accesses to CalculatorModel displayValue and enteringDecimal and Swift string assembly. The dispatcher selects this helper for observed decimal, sign and percent argument values.
findings.limitation: Decompiler temporary names and unresolved stubs limit the interpretation; the private Calculate.framework arithmetic itself was not decompiled for this report.

sections.title: Data and network boundary; rebuild scope

findings.claim: No URLSession resume event was observed during the three bounded flows
findings.explanation: Each completed flow stored network metadata with zero events in its tap window.
findings.limitation: Other network APIs, background requests and events outside the windows remain unknown; this is not proof that the App is entirely offline.

findings.claim: The three flows form a bounded rebuild target for an independent Calculator app
findings.explanation: The source playbooks and final labels give executable scenarios for decimal addition, signed addition and standalone percent. A clone must be installed and checked against those exact scripts on the same XR.
findings.limitation: The scientific landscape, history, memory, arbitrary precision, other operations, persistence and iOS 17/26 remain outside this acceptance scope.
